subject.title: [Bug] openclaw doctor reports memory search disabled but memory-core dreaming is running — conflicting status

question: Should `openclaw doctor` expose only independently enabled dreaming configuration, or should it also commit to reporting runtime last-run and next-scheduled status from memory-core?
rationale: The reporter requests operational scheduling details, but the closed candidate fixes demonstrate a narrower status note; choosing the enduring diagnostic surface requires maintainer product and plugin-contract intent.

options.title: Ship a bounded independent-status note
options.body: Keep memory-search output unchanged and add a separate dreaming enabled/phases/schedule section using currently authoritative data.

options.title: Define full runtime dreaming diagnostics
options.body: First specify a plugin-to-gateway status contract for last run, next schedule, and failure details, then implement it consistently in doctor and related status consumers.

options.title: Keep the current narrow doctor contract
options.body: Treat dreaming inspection as `openclaw memory status --deep` only and document that `doctor` reports embedding search separately.

recommendation.title: Ship a bounded independent-status note
recommendation.body: Keep memory-search output unchanged and add a separate dreaming enabled/phases/schedule section using currently authoritative data.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the gateway-health-to-doctor diagnostic boundary that would carry any supported runtime status.
